page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State Walli's formula for odd n
steps.margin_note: First mark. n=11 is odd, so the formula has NO trailing π/2.
steps.memory_tip: Odd n ⇒ no π/2; the descending products simply end at 2 (numerator) and 3 (denominator).
lines: When n is odd, ∫₀^(π/2) cosⁿx dx
steps.why: For an odd power, Walli's formula ends the descending products at 2 on top and 3 on the bottom, with no extra π/2 factor — unlike the even-n case.
common_mistakes: Attaching an extra π/2 factor that belongs only to the even-n version of the formula.
Stopping the descending product one term too early or too late.

steps.label: Substitute n=11 and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 3840/10395 simplifies to 256/693 after cancelling the common factor 15.
steps.memory_tip: For n=11 there are exactly five descending terms in both the numerator and denominator products.
steps.why: Substituting n=11 gives the descending product 10·8·6·4·2=3840 on top over 11·9·7·5·3=10395 on the bottom, which simplifies to 256/693.
common_mistakes: Missing a term in either the five-term numerator or denominator product.
Not simplifying the fraction 3840/10395 down to its lowest terms.
